claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and monitored 5% rollout plus rollback make release defensible, with the strongest admissible basis being explicit model-card disclosure of the still-exposed Spanish-language billing limitation.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for launch.
Policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
A reversible 5% rollout and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness but do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure predicate.
Public NIST and model-card guidance can support monitoring and documentation practices, but they do not substitute for the specific internal policy requirement.
evidence_requests: Provide the final model card or launch disclosure showing explicit disclosure of the Spanish-language billing support limitation for this release.
Provide evidence that the disclosure was reviewed and included in the pre-launch approval packet.
Provide an approved risk-acceptance record, if relied upon, signed by the approver and explicitly covering Spanish-language billing support exposure.
Provide evidence that the initial 5% cohort excludes the affected use case, if that is the mitigation being asserted instead of disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
specific_concerns: The affected Spanish-language billing support use case remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
Policy says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The available risk-acceptance draft is not approved because the approver line is blank.
The draft risk acceptance does not mention the exposed Spanish-language billing support segment.
No admissible evidence shows the required model-card disclosure has actually been prepared, reviewed, or attached to the launch decision.
The Actor's recommended action is stronger than the evidence because certification is framed as defensible only if explicit disclosure occurs, but that predicate is not evidenced.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently supported rather than conditionally supportable after explicit disclosure is completed.
That the strongest admissible defense for certification has already been satisfied.
Any implication that rollout controls plus monitoring are enough without either exclusion of the affected use case or approved risk acceptance or completed disclosure.
